title: Bus ticket booking in one transaction
scenario: A crash between saving the booking and its passengers left bookings with no passengers.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · plain JDBC transactions: auto-commit, commit, rollback · generated keys · batch insert · PostgreSQL 17 · Flyway · Testcontainers
simulation: Trips and fares are demo data, not Safarbus's. A booking is a record in this app's database; no payment is taken and no ticket is issued.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. A family books two seats

    The app saves the booking, then each passenger. Each insert is saved the moment it runs.

  2. Something fails in between

    The server restarts after the booking row, or seat 12 was taken a second earlier. The booking stays, charged for two seats, with one passenger or none. Support finds bookings no conductor can match to anyone.

  3. The fix

    Booking and passengers in one transaction: all rows are committed together, or a rollback removes them all.

Rows that only make sense together are saved together.

What are we building?

POST /bookings books up to six seats on a trip, one passenger per seat, and returns the booking id and total. If any seat is taken, nothing is booked.

An everyday analogy

A railway reservation form for a family: the clerk enters every name, and only then presses "confirm". If one berth is gone, the whole form comes back. Nobody gets a ticket for half a family.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Check the request: the trip exists, seats are on the bus and different.
  2. Begin: switch auto-commit off.
  3. Insert the booking (the database returns its id), then all passengers in one batch.
  4. Commit, or on any failure roll back: no half-booking either way.
Check yourself: why can't a CHECK constraint stop a booking with no passengers?

A CHECK looks at one row at a time. "This booking has at least one passenger" is about rows in another table, which are inserted after the booking. Only a transaction makes them appear together.

What this station is not

  • No payment. A confirmed booking is a record.
  • No seat hold. A seat is free or booked; holding it while someone pays is challenge 3.
  • No Spring @Transactional. Plain JDBC, so every step is visible; Spring does the same for you later.

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Safarbus (a fictional bus operator) found bookings with no passengers: a crash between saving the booking and its passengers left half-saved bookings.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given two passengers for seats 12 and 13 on trip 101, then 201, a new booking id, total ₹2,500.00, and two passenger rows.
  2. Given seats 11 and 12 when 12 is already booked, then 409 naming seat 12, and no new rows at all; seat 11 can be booked straight after.
  3. Given a failure after the booking row (a crash, a refused passenger, a Java error), then no booking row remains.
  4. Given seat 41 on a 40-seat bus, or the same seat twice, then 422; an unknown trip, 404.
  5. Given a bad phone, an age over 120, seat 0, no passengers, seven passengers, or an extra field, then 400.

Requirements

  • The booking and its passengers are written in one transaction.
  • One seat on one trip belongs to one booking: a database constraint decides, so two people racing for it cannot both win.
  • A passenger's trip is always its booking's trip (a composite foreign key).
  • Money in integer paise; the total is fare × passengers.

Learning objectives

  • Turn auto-commit off, commit, and roll back with plain JDBC.
  • Read a generated key after an insert.
  • Insert many rows with a JDBC batch.
  • Turn a constraint violation into a clear 409.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Auto-commit on: a crash leaves a booking without its passengers.

The old code runs against the real PostgreSQL. A crash between the two inserts leaves a booking with no passengers. A taken seat halfway leaves a booking charged for two seats with one passenger. The real store, given the same failure, leaves nothing. While building, each fix was undone once. Leaving auto-commit on turned 8 tests red. Removing the rollback turned only 1 red, and only after a test was added for a Java error midway. PostgreSQL will not commit a transaction in which a statement failed, but setAutoCommit(true) in the finally block commits a transaction that had no database error. Not restoring auto-commit was not caught, because HikariCP resets it when the connection returns to the pool. The line stays, so the code does not depend on the pool.

package com.safarbus.bookings;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.sql.SQLException;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/** The first test written for this station: the old code's half-saved bookings, on the real database. */
class AutoCommitTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void aCrashAfterTheBookingRowLeavesABookingWithNoPassengers() throws Exception {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> OldBookingStore.save(dataSource, trip101(), "9876543210", seats(4, 5),
                () -> { throw new IllegalStateException("crash between the two inserts"); }))
                .hasMessage("crash between the two inserts");
        assertThat(bookingsWithoutPassengers()).isEqualTo(1);
    }

    @Test
    void aTakenSeatHalfwayLeavesHalfABooking() throws Exception {
        store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", seats(5));
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> OldBookingStore.save(dataSource, trip101(), "9123456780", seats(4, 5), () -> { }))
                .isInstanceOf(SQLException.class);
        // The second booking exists, charged for two seats, with seat 4 only.
        assertThat(bookings()).isEqualTo(2);
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM booking_passengers WHERE booking_id = 2").query(Long.class).single()).isEqualTo(1);
    }

    @Test
    void inOneTransactionTheSameFailureLeavesNothing() throws Exception {
        store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", seats(5));
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> store.save(trip101(), "9123456780", seats(4, 5))).isInstanceOf(SQLException.class);
        assertThat(bookings()).isEqualTo(1);
        assertThat(passengers()).isEqualTo(1);
        assertThat(bookingsWithoutPassengers()).isZero();
    }
}
package com.safarbus.bookings;

import javax.sql.DataSource;
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;

/** The booking code before the fix, kept only in tests: auto-commit on, so every statement commits by itself. */
final class OldBookingStore {

    private OldBookingStore() {
    }

    /** afterBooking runs between the two inserts: the moment a crash or a timeout would hit. */
    static long save(DataSource dataSource, Trip trip, String phone, List<Passenger> passengers, Runnable afterBooking) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            long bookingId;
            try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", new String[]{"id"})) {
                s.setLong(1, trip.id());
                s.setString(2, phone);
                s.setLong(3, trip.farePaise() * passengers.size());
                s.executeUpdate();   // committed now
                try (ResultSet keys = s.getGeneratedKeys()) {
                    keys.next();
                    bookingId = keys.getLong(1);
                }
            }
            afterBooking.run();
            for (Passenger p : passengers) {
                try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                        "INSERT INTO booking_passengers (booking_id, trip_id, seat_no, name, age, fare_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")) {
                    s.setLong(1, bookingId);
                    s.setLong(2, trip.id());
                    s.setInt(3, p.seatNo());
                    s.setString(4, p.name());
                    s.setInt(5, p.age());
                    s.setLong(6, trip.farePaise());
                    s.executeUpdate();   // each passenger committed on its own
                }
            }
            return bookingId;
        }
    }
}

package com.safarbus.bookings;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ResponseStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

@RestController
class BookingController {

    record BookingRequest(@NotNull Long tripId,
                          @NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "[6-9]\\d{9}", message = "must be a 10-digit Indian mobile number") String contactPhone,
                          @NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 6) List<@NotNull @Valid Passenger> passengers) {
    }

    record BookingResponse(long bookingId, long tripId, List<Integer> seats, long totalPaise, String status) {
    }

    private final Trips trips;
    private final BookingStore store;

    BookingController(Trips trips, BookingStore store) {
        this.trips = trips;
        this.store = store;
    }

    /** Records a booking (a demo booking record; no payment is taken). */
    @PostMapping("/bookings")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    BookingResponse book(@Valid @RequestBody BookingRequest request) throws SQLException {
        Trip trip = trips.find(request.tripId()).orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Trip not found", "No trip " + request.tripId() + "."));
        List<Integer> seats = request.passengers().stream().map(Passenger::seatNo).toList();
        if (seats.stream().distinct().count() != seats.size()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Same seat twice", "Each passenger needs a different seat.");
        }
        if (seats.stream().anyMatch(s -> s > trip.seats())) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "No such seat", "Trip " + trip.id() + " has seats 1 to " + trip.seats() + ".");
        }
        try {
            long bookingId = store.save(trip, request.contactPhone(), request.passengers());
            return new BookingResponse(bookingId, trip.id(), seats, trip.farePaise() * seats.size(), "CONFIRMED");
        } catch (SQLException e) {
            if (BookingStore.violates(e, "booking_passengers_seat_once")) {
                // The database decided, so two people racing for one seat cannot both win.
                List<Integer> taken = store.taken(trip.id(), seats);
                String which = taken.stream().map(String::valueOf).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
                throw problem(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "Seat already booked", (taken.size() == 1 ? "Seat " + which + " is" : "Seats " + which + " are")
                        + " already booked on trip " + trip.id() + ". Nothing was booked.");
            }
            throw e;
        }
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/safarbus/bookings/BookingStore.java

Does
Saves a booking and its passengers as one transaction.
Why
Auto-commit off, two inserts, commit; rollback on any failure; auto-commit restored.
Without it
The trap: every insert committed on its own.
  • prepareStatement(sql, new String[]{"id"}) asks the driver to return the new id.
  • The passengers go as one batch: one statement, six rows, one round trip.
  • Calling setAutoCommit(true) during a transaction commits it, which is why the rollback must come first.
package com.safarbus.bookings;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository;

import javax.sql.DataSource;
import java.sql.Array;
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Saves a booking and its passengers as one unit. Auto-commit is switched off, so the booking row and every passenger
 * row become visible together at commit, or, after any failure, not at all.
 */
@Repository
class BookingStore {

    private final DataSource dataSource;

    BookingStore(DataSource dataSource) {
        this.dataSource = dataSource;
    }

    long save(Trip trip, String phone, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            c.setAutoCommit(false);
            try {
                long bookingId = insertBooking(c, trip, phone, trip.farePaise() * passengers.size());
                insertPassengers(c, bookingId, trip, passengers);
                c.commit();
                return bookingId;
            } catch (SQLException | RuntimeException e) {
                c.rollback();   // the booking row goes too: nothing half-saved
                throw e;
            } finally {
                c.setAutoCommit(true);   // the pool lends this connection out again next
            }
        }
    }

    /** The database creates the id; RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS for the "id" column hands it back. */
    private static long insertBooking(Connection c, Trip trip, String phone, long totalPaise) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", new String[]{"id"})) {
            s.setLong(1, trip.id());
            s.setString(2, phone);
            s.setLong(3, totalPaise);
            s.executeUpdate();
            try (ResultSet keys = s.getGeneratedKeys()) {
                keys.next();
                return keys.getLong(1);
            }
        }
    }

    /** One statement, one row per passenger, sent to the database as a batch: one round trip, not six. */
    private static void insertPassengers(Connection c, long bookingId, Trip trip, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                "INSERT INTO booking_passengers (booking_id, trip_id, seat_no, name, age, fare_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")) {
            for (Passenger p : passengers) {
                s.setLong(1, bookingId);
                s.setLong(2, trip.id());
                s.setInt(3, p.seatNo());
                s.setString(4, p.name().strip());
                s.setInt(5, p.age());
                s.setLong(6, trip.farePaise());
                s.addBatch();
            }
            s.executeBatch();
        }
    }

    /** Which of these seats are already booked on the trip. */
    List<Integer> taken(long tripId, List<Integer> seats) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection();
             PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement("SELECT seat_no FROM booking_passengers WHERE trip_id = ? AND seat_no = ANY (?) ORDER BY seat_no")) {
            Array array = c.createArrayOf("integer", seats.toArray());
            s.setLong(1, tripId);
            s.setArray(2, array);
            try (ResultSet r = s.executeQuery()) {
                List<Integer> found = new ArrayList<>();
                while (r.next()) {
                    found.add(r.getInt(1));
                }
                return found;
            }
        }
    }

    /** A unique violation (SQLState 23505) of this constraint. PostgreSQL's driver puts both on the batch's own exception. */
    static boolean violates(SQLException e, String constraint) {
        return "23505".equals(e.getSQLState()) && String.valueOf(e.getMessage()).contains(constraint);
    }
}

    Optional<Trip> find(long id) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection();
             PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement("SELECT id, route, seats, fare_paise FROM trips WHERE id = ?")) {
            s.setLong(1, id);
            try (ResultSet r = s.executeQuery()) {
                return r.next() ? Optional.of(new Trip(r.getLong("id"), r.getString("route"), r.getInt("seats"), r.getLong("fare_paise"))) : Optional.empty();
            }
        }
    }
}

package com.safarbus.bookings;

import com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariDataSource;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.DriverManager;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/** The database's rules with Java bypassed, and what commit, rollback and a dead connection do. */
class BookingDatabaseTest extends ApiTest {

    void sql(Connection c, String sql) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(sql)) {
            s.executeUpdate();
        }
    }

    @Test
    void namedConstraintsHoldWithoutJava() throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            sql(c, "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (101, '9876543210', 125000)");   // booking 1
            sql(c, "INSERT INTO booking_passengers VALUES (1, 101, 7, 'A', 30, 125000)");
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> sql(c, "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (101, '12345', 125000)"))
                    .hasMessageContaining("bookings_phone_digits");
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> sql(c, "INSERT INTO booking_passengers VALUES (1, 101, 8, 'B', 130, 125000)"))
                    .hasMessageContaining("booking_passengers_age_range");
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> sql(c, "INSERT INTO booking_passengers VALUES (1, 102, 9, 'C', 30, 125000)"))
                    .hasMessageContaining("booking_passengers_booking_fk");   // a passenger on another trip than its booking
        }
    }

    @Test
    void oneSeatOnOneTripBelongsToOneBookingOnly() throws Exception {
        store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", seats(7));
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            sql(c, "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (101, '9123456780', 125000)");   // booking 2
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> sql(c, "INSERT INTO booking_passengers VALUES (2, 101, 7, 'B', 30, 125000)"))
                    .hasMessageContaining("booking_passengers_seat_once");
        }
    }

    @Test
    void aDeadConnectionCommitsNothing() throws SQLException {
        HikariDataSource pool = (HikariDataSource) dataSource;   // a connection of its own, outside the pool, to kill
        Connection c = DriverManager.getConnection(pool.getJdbcUrl(), pool.getUsername(), pool.getPassword());
        c.setAutoCommit(false);
        sql(c, "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (101, '9876543210', 125000)");
        c.abort(Runnable::run);   // the process dies before commit: the server rolls the transaction back
        assertThat(bookings()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void aRefusedPassengerRollsBackTheWholeBooking() throws Exception {
        List<Passenger> oneTooOld = List.of(new Passenger("Fine", 30, 1), new Passenger("Refused by the database", 130, 2));
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", oneTooOld)).hasMessageContaining("booking_passengers_age_range");
        assertThat(bookings()).isZero();
        assertThat(passengers()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void aJavaErrorMidwayRollsBackToo() throws Exception {
        // A passenger with no name fails in Java (strip() on null) after the booking row is inserted. Without the
        // rollback, the finally block's setAutoCommit(true) would commit that booking: JDBC commits on that call.
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", List.of(new Passenger(null, 30, 1))))
                .isInstanceOf(NullPointerException.class);
        assertThat(bookings()).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void generatedIdsComeBackAndTheBatchSavesEveryRow() throws Exception {
        long first = store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", seats(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6));
        long second = store.save(trip101(), "9876543210", seats(7));
        assertThat(second).isEqualTo(first + 1);
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT seat_no FROM booking_passengers WHERE booking_id = ? ORDER BY seat_no").param(first).query(Integer.class).list())
                .containsExactly(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
    }
}

package com.safarbus.bookings;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository;

import javax.sql.DataSource;
import java.sql.Array;
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Saves a booking and its passengers as one unit. Auto-commit is switched off, so the booking row and every passenger
 * row become visible together at commit, or, after any failure, not at all.
 */
@Repository
class BookingStore {

    private final DataSource dataSource;

    BookingStore(DataSource dataSource) {
        this.dataSource = dataSource;
    }

    long save(Trip trip, String phone, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            c.setAutoCommit(false);
            try {
                long bookingId = insertBooking(c, trip, phone, passengers.stream().mapToLong(p -> fare(trip, p)).sum());
                insertPassengers(c, bookingId, trip, passengers);
                c.commit();
                return bookingId;
            } catch (SQLException | RuntimeException e) {
                c.rollback();   // the booking row goes too: nothing half-saved
                throw e;
            } finally {
                c.setAutoCommit(true);   // the pool lends this connection out again next
            }
        }
    }

    /** The database creates the id; RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS for the "id" column hands it back. */
    private static long insertBooking(Connection c, Trip trip, String phone, long totalPaise) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", new String[]{"id"})) {
            s.setLong(1, trip.id());
            s.setString(2, phone);
            s.setLong(3, totalPaise);
            s.executeUpdate();
            try (ResultSet keys = s.getGeneratedKeys()) {
                keys.next();
                return keys.getLong(1);
            }
        }
    }

    /** One statement, one row per passenger, sent to the database as a batch: one round trip, not six. */
    private static void insertPassengers(Connection c, long bookingId, Trip trip, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                "INSERT INTO booking_passengers (booking_id, trip_id, seat_no, name, age, fare_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")) {
            for (Passenger p : passengers) {
                s.setLong(1, bookingId);
                s.setLong(2, trip.id());
                s.setInt(3, p.seatNo());
                s.setString(4, p.name().strip());
                s.setInt(5, p.age());
                s.setLong(6, fare(trip, p));
                s.addBatch();
            }
            s.executeBatch();
        }
    }

    /** Demo rule: 60 and over pay 75%, rounded to the nearest paisa, half up. */
    static long fare(Trip trip, Passenger p) {
        return p.age() >= 60 ? (trip.farePaise() * 75 + 50) / 100 : trip.farePaise();
    }

package com.safarbus.bookings;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository;

import java.sql.Array;
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.PreparedStatement;
import java.sql.ResultSet;
import java.sql.SQLException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Saves a booking and its passengers as one unit. Auto-commit is switched off, so the booking row and every passenger
 * row become visible together at commit, or, after any failure, not at all.
 */
@Repository
class BookingStore {

    private final DataSource dataSource;

    BookingStore(DataSource dataSource) {
        this.dataSource = dataSource;
    }

    long save(Trip trip, String phone, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {
        try (Connection c = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            c.setAutoCommit(false);
            try {
                long bookingId = insertBooking(c, trip, phone, passengers.stream().mapToLong(p -> fare(trip, p)).sum());
                insertPassengers(c, bookingId, trip, passengers);
                c.commit();
                return bookingId;
            } catch (SQLException | RuntimeException e) {
                c.rollback();   // the booking row goes too: nothing half-saved
                throw e;
            } finally {
                c.setAutoCommit(true);   // the pool lends this connection out again next
            }
        }
    }

    /** The database creates the id; RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS for the "id" column hands it back. */
    private static long insertBooking(Connection c, Trip trip, String phone, long totalPaise) throws SQLException {
        try (PreparedStatement s = c.prepareStatement(
                "INSERT INTO bookings (trip_id, contact_phone, total_paise) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", new String[]{"id"})) {
            s.setLong(1, trip.id());
            s.setString(2, phone);
            s.setLong(3, totalPaise);
            s.executeUpdate();
            try (ResultSet keys = s.getGeneratedKeys()) {
                keys.next();
                return keys.getLong(1);
            }
        }
    }

    private static void insertPassengers(Connection c, long bookingId, Trip trip, List<Passenger> passengers) throws SQLException {

                s.setLong(2, trip.id());
                s.setInt(3, p.seatNo());
                s.setString(4, p.name().strip());
                s.setInt(5, p.age());

            }

CREATE TABLE trips (
    id          BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    route       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    departs_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,
    seats       SMALLINT     NOT NULL,
    fare_paise  BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT trips_seats_range   CHECK (seats BETWEEN 1 AND 60),
    CONSTRAINT trips_fare_positive CHECK (fare_paise > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE bookings (
    id            BIGINT      GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    trip_id       BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    contact_phone CHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
    total_paise   BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT bookings_trip_fk        FOREIGN KEY (trip_id) REFERENCES trips (id),
    CONSTRAINT bookings_phone_digits   CHECK (contact_phone ~ '^[6-9][0-9]{9}$'),
    CONSTRAINT bookings_total_positive CHECK (total_paise > 0),

    CONSTRAINT bookings_id_trip_unique UNIQUE (id, trip_id)
);

Interview takeaways

What is auto-commit in JDBC?

The default mode: each statement runs in its own transaction and commits immediately. For several statements that belong together, switch it off, commit at the end, and roll back on failure.

What happens if you call setAutoCommit(true) in the middle of a transaction?

The JDBC specification says the transaction is committed. That is why the rollback must happen before auto-commit is restored.

How do you get a generated id after an insert?

prepareStatement(sql, new String[]{"id"}) or Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS, then getGeneratedKeys() after executeUpdate(). In PostgreSQL, INSERT ... RETURNING id does the same in SQL.

Why a batch insert?

One statement, many parameter sets, sent together: fewer round trips. Inside a transaction, a failing row fails the batch and the rollback undoes it all.

Who should decide that a seat is free, Java or the database?

The database, with a unique constraint. A Java check followed by an insert has a gap where another request can take the seat.
